# Exact optimization of the gamma-only single-template shell certificate on boxes

This note evaluates a particular proved sufficient certificate. It does not
refute OC. All original mass stays in the denominator, and the upper bound
accounts for every convex template, every affine copy-center map, and every
contained choice of radii. The six-dimensional obstruction below is ONLY
to the certificate with the universal constant Gamma_d. Exact ordinary
own-fiber depth already repairs that example; the stronger shape-aware
obstruction is in `candidate 2d5ed8c78661db43`.

## 1. The menu and the actual three-fiber body

Let d>=1. Let A and B be axis-parallel boxes in R^d with strictly positive
side lengths a_i and b_i. Their translations are arbitrary. Put K=(A+B)/2
and C=conv(({-1} times A) union ({1} times B)). Then C is an ambient
convex body, its only integer fibers are A,K,B, and its mixed mass is
M=|A|+|K|+|B|. All fibers are full dimensional, so q=d and mixed volume
is exactly the intrinsic measure in the task.

Choose any centroid-zero convex body J of volume V>0, any affine map
c:R->R^d, and radii r_-,r_0,r_+>=0. Every positive-radius copy
c(j)+r_j J must be contained in the corresponding fiber. Zero radius
asserts no containment. A candidate Y=(p,c(p)) is expressly required to
belong to S, p in {-1,0,1}. Set w_j=r_j^d, with weights zero elsewhere.
Write D_p(w) for closed-halfspace atomic depth on the integer base and
R_p(w) for the sum of the smaller weights in reflected pairs about p.

The proved shell theorem in
`candidate 4d7e8cb4ef98b96f` gives
the raw certificate Gamma_d V[D_p(w)+R_p(w)]. Here we optimize this
specific expression, without replacing its own contribution by a better
ordinary-depth bound.

At an endpoint p, D_p=w_p and R_p=0. At p=0,

    D_0=w_0+min(w_-,w_+),   R_0=min(w_-,w_+).       (1)

These statements include zero weights and closed boundary atoms: a base
halfspace in one dimension contains its anchor and one of the two sides.

## 2. An exact finite formula for all templates

Define

    c_i=min(a_i,b_i),   m_i=(a_i+b_i)/2,
    rho_i=m_i/c_i>=1,   k=product_i m_i.

For s>0 put

    G(s)=(s^d+2) product_i min(c_i,m_i/s).           (2)

Then the exact supremum of V[D_p+R_p] over all the above choices is

    max{|A|,|B|, max_{i=1,...,d} G(rho_i)}.        (3)

In particular the supremum is attained by a legitimate template and
affine center graph. There is no unproved optimizer-existence assertion.

Proof of the universal upper bound. At endpoint anchors, containment
gives Vw_p<=|K_p|. At the middle, put r=min(r_-,r_+). If r>0 and r_0>0,
let T=rJ and s=r_0/r. Since 0 is in J, each smaller copy rJ is contained
in its original larger endpoint copy. Translated copies of T therefore
fit inside A and B, and a translate of sT fits inside K. Coordinate
width is translation invariant, so

    width_i(T)<=min(c_i,m_i/s).

Any body lies in its coordinate bounding box, hence its volume is at
most the product of these widths. Formula (1) now bounds the middle
coefficient by G(s). If r=0, it is at most k. If r_0=0, it is at most
2 product c_i; both bounds are included in max_s G(s), since G is
strictly larger than k at s=max rho_i and larger than 2 product c_i
at s=min rho_i. Thus zero radii introduce no exception.

To reduce max_s to finitely many values, sort the rho_i. Below the
smallest breakpoint, G(s)=(s^d+2) product c_i is increasing. Above the
largest it is k(1+2/s^d), which is decreasing. On any intervening
interval with exactly j coordinates having rho_i<=s, put x=log s.
For a positive constant C depending on that interval,

    G(exp x)=C[exp((d-j)x)+2 exp(-j x)].             (4)

Its second derivative is nonnegative, so its maximum on that closed
interval is at an endpoint. Repeated breakpoints cause no difficulty.
This proves the claimed finite upper bound.

For equality at any s, take T to be the centered box with side lengths
min(c_i,m_i/s), use radius1 in the two endpoint fibers and radius s in
the middle. Choose c(j) to be their actual box centers; the center of K
is the average of the centers of A and B, so these three centers are
one affine graph. Every containment holds coordinatewise, and the
middle coefficient is exactly G(s). Endpoint values are attained by
taking its whole centered fiber as template and zero other radii.
This proves (3). Notice that the upper argument allowed even unrelated
translations, which makes its all-affine-graphs scope immediate.

## 3. An exact six-dimensional failure of the gamma-only menu

Set d=6. Let A be the centered box with side lengths

    (2,2,2,1/2,1/2,1/2)

and let B be the centered unit cube. Then |A|=|B|=1. Their midpoint K
has side lengths (3/2,3/2,3/2,3/4,3/4,3/4), so

    k=729/512,   M=1753/512.

The maximal coordinatewise common box E has side lengths
(1,1,1,1/2,1/2,1/2), volume t=1/8, and K=(3/2)E. All six rho_i equal
3/2, so (3) gives the EXACT optimized coefficient

    max_{J,c,r,p} V[D_p+R_p]=k+2t=857/512.          (5)

The original OC coefficient is M/2=1753/1024, which is larger by

    1753/1024-857/512=39/1024>0.                   (6)

Consequently every gamma-only certificate, even after optimizing all
templates, core radii, affine centers and actual anchors, falls strictly
below the original OC target by Gamma_6*39/1024. Equality in (5) uses
J=E, zero centers, endpoint radii1 and middle radius3/2.

This is a certificate obstruction, not a depth obstruction. At the
middle box center the own fiber alone has raw depth k/2. In fact

    k/2-Gamma_6 M/2=3978153/120472576>0,
    Gamma_6=(6/7)^6=46656/117649.                   (7)

Thus using exact own-fiber depth already proves OC for this example.
It would be incorrect to cite (5) as an obstruction to that stronger
menu or to shape-specific paired-tail constants.

## 4. A positive planar calibration

For equal-area axis-parallel rectangles, divide out the common area and
apply a determinant-one diagonal map. Up to interchanging coordinates,
their normalized side lengths may be written (R,1/R) and (1,1), R>=1.
The common box has volume1/R, while

    k=(R+2+1/R)/4.

The two rho_i are equal to (R+1)/2, so the exact middle coefficient in
(3) is k+2/R. It strictly exceeds the original target coefficient:

    k+2/R-(k+2)/2
       =(R^2-6R+17)/(8R)=((R-3)^2+8)/(8R)>0.      (8)

Hence this template menu does suffice for every equal-area pair of
axis-parallel planar rectangles and their exact Minkowski middle,
including arbitrary translations. This observation does not extend
the failed high-dimensional assertion to arbitrary shapes.
